title: Why Harder To Buy Means Better Customers
hook_text: MAKING IT HARDER TO BUY BRINGS BETTER BUYERS

beats.say: Making something harder to buy can bring better buyers.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a brass door lock turning in cold blue dusk light.

beats.say: If you want clients who never ask for refunds, why do you make checkout so easy?
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a heavy steel gate sliding shut on a rain-slick street.

beats.say: Most people assume fewer steps mean more sales.
beats.visual: Wide silhouette of a lone commuter walking past glowing storefronts at night.

beats.say: That is wrong. According to Alex Hormozi, adding checkout qualifications weeds out cheap leads who drain your time.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a fountain pen signing a dark contract under sodium lights.

beats.say: How do you filter out bad buyers without killing your revenue?
beats.visual: High angle shot of empty highway lanes cutting through a concrete overpass.

beats.say: Get sales flowing first, then add friction so you don't filter out zero volume.
beats.visual: Close-up of a single practical light bulb swinging in a dark, damp concrete room.

beats.say: Every extra question and qualification cuts volume but raises buyer quality.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a solitary figure standing on a massive concrete dam at dusk.

beats.say: What is the honest catch for building a business this way?
beats.visual: Low angle shot of rusted iron girders under a heavy grey fog.

beats.say: About 1 in 5 US businesses close in their first year, and close to half by year five.
beats.visual: Close-up of a weathered brick wall struck by cold morning light.

beats.say: This requires massive effort, and nobody can promise your results.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a lone worker climbing an industrial tower against a dark sky.

beats.say: This week, add one qualification question to your checkout form.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a mechanical timer ticking down on a dark metal desk.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: Wide shot of a single amber light cutting through a deep urban fog.

caption: Making something harder to buy brings better buyers. #moneypsychology #businessgrowth #personalfinance #wealthmindset #financialfreedom
description: Learn why adding friction to your checkout process can weed out cheap leads and attract higher-quality customers.
first_comment: Would you add friction to your offer if it meant higher-paying customers?

facts.claim: About 1 in 5 US businesses close in their first year and close to half by year five
facts.basis: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Business Employment Dynamics

loop_map.stakes: Your checkout process and customer quality are at risk.
loop_map.big_question: How do you filter out bad buyers without killing your revenue?
loop_map.reveal: Adding checkout qualifications weeds out cheap leads.
